scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
**Executive summary** — read as an Executive summary per `references/artifact-patterns.md`.

Every month your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems stay on 28 on-premises SQL Server instances spread across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines, you carry $1,850,000 in annual technology spend as a fixed cost tied to infrastructure you own and operate directly [PF-2.13 GAP: no stated current run-rate breakdown by system or vendor — reduction target not yet quantified by the buyer]. That exposure sharpens now: your DOT compliance audit opens in six months, and an on-premises estate of this size is the surface auditors will examine most closely. Migrating load-matching and carrier-settlement onto Google Cloud — Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer — replaces that fixed infrastructure footprint with a managed platform before the audit window opens, giving you a materially different position to walk into that review with than the one you hold today.

The programme runs two years at a stated cost of $4,200,000, moving you from 28 self-managed SQL Server instances on Hyper-V to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, and from 620 self-managed virtual machines to Google Compute Engine [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm the $4,200,000 figure and 2-year duration are the approved programme baseline, not an estimate, before this ships]. You should expect this document's team to report progress against the two measures you've said you're accountable for — the technology spend it replaces and the compliance posture it changes going into your audit — rather than against infrastructure milestones alone [PF-2.11 GAP: no post-migration spend target or percentage reduction has been supplied; state only once you provide a figure, or confirm none exists to report].

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| [PF-2.13 GAP] | PF-2.13 | The $1,850,000 baseline's composition and any stated reduction target — confirm whether a specific savings figure exists to cite. |
| [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment)] | PF-2.14 | Confirm the $4,200,000 / 2-year programme figures are an approved commitment, not a rough estimate, before this ships as a promise to the CFO. |
| [PF-2.11 GAP] | PF-2.11 | No post-migration cost-reduction number was supplied — either provide one or confirm the summary should stay silent on a specific target. |
